fields.explanation: Preserves exactly the original five distinct three-element sets on nine atoms, M={m1,m2}, and real LP weights 0,0,1/3,1/3,1/3. Uses Mathlib Finset cardinality, pairwise Disjoint and finite sums. Exhausts all Finset (Fin 5) subfamilies to prove M is a maximum packing and no finite exchange improves M; this implies the source local optimality at every radius. Every subfamily has total nonnegative real weight at most one, a stronger condition than all intersecting-family LP and element constraints. Positive support is proved exactly, and F2 is derived by two actual intersections with M. The auxiliary multigraph is the actual Mathlib Graph.banana with three independently indexed edges; the source incidence relation is proved equivalent to F2 membership plus intersection with both distinct matching sets. Its induced graph on all M has three internal edges and two vertices, but the corresponding original family is not pairwise disjoint. The final refutation theorem explicitly denies that this edge excess supplies an improving packing. No source assumption is omitted from the stored challenged passage, and the valid witness is unchanged.
fields.flaw: Let \(I=(\mathcal U,\mathcal C)\) be a \(k\)-set-packing instance with \(|\mathcal C|=n\), let \(\varepsilon>0\), and let \(M\subseteq\mathcal C\) be a \(4(1+1/\varepsilon)\log_2 n\)-locally optimal matching (that is, a packing of mutually disjoint sets). Let \(x\) be any feasible solution to the intersecting-family LP, let \(\mathcal F=\{f\in\mathcal C:x_f>0\}\), and let \(\mathcal F_2\) consist of those \(f\in\mathcal F\) that intersect exactly two members of \(M\). Define the auxiliary undirected multigraph \(H\) to have one vertex \(v_m\) for every \(m\in M\) and one edge \(e_f\) for every \(f\in\mathcal F_2\), joining \(v_{m_1}\) and \(v_{m_2}\) when \(m_1,m_2\) are the two members of \(M\) intersected by \(f\); distinct members of \(\mathcal F_2\) may therefore give parallel edges. For every \(X\subseteq V(H)\), let \(\mathcal B_X=\{f\in\mathcal F_2:e_f\in E(H[X])\}\). If \(|E(H[X])|>|X|\), then \(\mathcal B_X\) is an improving set for \(M\): \(\mathcal B_X\) is a packing and, in the intersection graph \(G\) of the packings \(M\) and \(\mathcal B_X\), \(N_G(B_X,M)=N(B_X)\cap M\) and \(\left|(M\cup B_X)\setminus N_G(B_X,M)\right|>|M|\). Equivalently, adding the source sets corresponding to the edges of \(H[X]\) and removing the members of \(M\) that they intersect yields a mutually disjoint solution of larger cardinality.
fields.problem: Title: On local search and LP and SDP relaxations for k-Set Packing
fields.source_context:
0001 | [Original v1 source: Terminology and local-optimality definitions]
0002 | We proceed with some notational conventions and definitions to make sure no confusion may arise.
0003 | By $\mathcal{U}$ we mean the universe of elements over which the $k$-set system $\mathcal{C} \subseteq 2^{\mathcal{U}}$ has been defined. We write $|\mathcal{U}| = N$ and $|\mathcal{C}| = n$. By $I = (\mathcal{U},\mathcal{C})$ a given instance for $k$-set packing is denoted in which the objective is to find the largest packing.
0004 | 
0005 | \begin{defn}
0006 | \textbf{(Conflict graph)} Let an instance $I = (\mathcal{U},\mathcal{C})$ for the $k$-set packing problem be given. The conflict graph of $I$ is the graph $G$ where every subset in $\mathcal{C}$ is represented by a vertex. Two vertices
0007 | are adjacent if and only if
0008 | the subsets in $\mathcal{C}$ these vertices correspond to intersect each other.
0009 | \end{defn}
0010 | 
0011 | Now let $\mathcal{A}$ be some solution to this instance, i.e. a collection of subsets in $\mathcal{C}$ that are mutually disjoint.
0012 | 
0013 | \begin{defn}
0014 | \textbf{(Intersection graph)} Let an instance $I$ for the $k$-set packing problem be given and let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be two packings. The intersection graph of $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ is the induced subgraph of their vertices in the conflict graph of $I$.
0015 | \end{defn}
fields.witness: Take k=3, ε=1, U={a1,a2,a3,b1,b2,b3,c1,c2,c3}, m1={a1,a2,a3}, m2={b1,b2,b3}, and fi={a1,b1,ci} for i=1,2,3. Let C={m1,m2,f1,f2,f3}, n=5, M={m1,m2}, and x_fi=1/3, x_mj=0. Then F=F2={f1,f2,f3}. For X=V(H), H[X] has two vertices and three parallel edges, so |E(H[X])|=3>|X|=2. Nevertheless all fi share a1 and b1, so B_X is not a packing.
